result.summary: This PR implements BIP95 (Testnet 5), a new test network that drops the 20-minute minimum-difficulty exception used on testnet3/4, raises minimum difficulty, and enforces BIP54 (Consensus Cleanup) from genesis. It adds a new ChainType/chain selection option, kernel API support, chainparams, and documentation, and the diff also carries the full BIP54 implementation (sigops consensus check, timewarp fix, coinbase timelock, 64-byte-tx invalidity) because the PR is based on the still-open #35793. The author states only the top five commits are genuinely new here; the rest will disappear once #35793 lands and this PR is rebased.
result.problem: Testnet3 and testnet4 are frequently disrupted by trivial minimum-difficulty mining, and there is no live network to exercise the proposed BIP54 consensus-cleanup rules before any mainnet activation decision. Developers and the BIP54 proposal itself need a real test network to validate the rules and tooling (e.g. a solo-mining ckpool endpoint) ahead of a possible future soft fork.

result.card: This draft PR implements BIP95 Testnet 5, a new test network that removes testnet3/4's easy minimum-difficulty exception and enforces BIP54 (Consensus Cleanup) from block 1, with the genesis block not yet mined. It depends on the still-open #35793 (BIP54 implementation), and the author explicitly says the PR should stay in draft until that lands, though reviewers can review the design now. The diff is large because it includes #35793's BIP54 consensus logic and tests, but the author states only the top five commits (chain-type plumbing, kernel API entry, BIP54 activation, and docs) are unique to this PR. No reviewer has commented yet, and CI is failing with a needed rebase. Its main value is providing a live network for the community and pool operators to exercise BIP54 ahead of any mainnet activation decision, but it carries no release-blocking stakes since it explicitly will miss the v32 feature freeze.
